message.content:
I don’t have direct access to VirusTotal’s live database right now, so I can’t pull up the exact CAA record set for **instagram.com** myself. However, you can easily obtain that information using your own API key (`ig_key001`) by following one of the methods below:

---

### Method 1 – Using `curl` (Command‑Line)

```bash
curl -X GET \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/instagram.com/dns_records/CaaRecord \
     -H "x-apikey: ig_key001"
```

*Replace `ig_key001` with your actual API key.*

This will return JSON similar to:

```json
{
    "data": [
        {
            "_id": "...",
            "attributes": {
                "name": "instagram.com.",
                "value": "0 issue \"letsencrypt.org\";",
                ...
            }
        },
        …
    ]
}
```

If there are multiple CAA entries, each will appear under `"data"`.

---

### Method 2 – Using Python & Requests

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/instagram.com/dns_records/CaaRecord"
headers = {"x-apikey": "ig_key001"}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
print(response.json())
```

Make sure you’ve installed `requests` (`pip install requests`). This script prints out all CAA records returned by VT.

---

### Things To Keep In Mind

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Rate Limits** | Free tier allows ~60 queries per minute. If you hit the limit, wait a few seconds before retrying. |
| **API Key Security** | Never expose your key publicly. Store it securely (e.g., environment variable). |
| **Response Format** | Results come back in JSON. Look inside the `"data"` array for individual DNS records. |

---

#### Quick Test

If you want a quick sanity check without writing code, try visiting:

<https://www.virustotal.com/gui/domain/instagram.com>  

Scroll down to “DNS Records” → “CAA”. That page shows exactly what the API would return.

---
